title: Conjectural certainty: signs that secure the mind without banishing all fear
source_text: V. Tertium gradum habent illa quae tot signis & conjecturis nituntur, ut securum hominem reddant, & anxietatem expellant, non tamen excludant omnem formidinem. Atque haec dicitur certitudo conjecturalis, & opinionis est potius quam fidei. Veluti quum quis ex stylo atque dicendi modo, sive ex ipsis characterum ductibus, agnoscit epistolam, aut librum ab aliquo scriptum; vel ex variis indiciis colligit aegrum aliquem tali, vel tali morbo laborare.
pass_a_gloss: The third degree belongs to those things which rest on so many signs and conjectures that they render a person secure and drive out anxiety, yet do not exclude all fear. And this is called conjectural certainty, and belongs to opinion rather than to faith—as when someone from style and manner of speaking, or from the very strokes of the characters, recognizes a letter or book written by someone; or from various indications gathers that a sick person labors under this or that disease.
pass_b_english: Lowest obscure certainty is conjectural: many signs quiet anxiety without removing every fear.
Handwriting recognition and medical diagnosis illustrate this opinion-level certainty.
